answer:
Use OpenFOAM with the compressible density-based solver rhoCentralFoam.
Treat air as a perfect gas with hePsiThermo, perfectGas equation of state, and Sutherland transport.
Use a two-dimensional planar mesh extruded one cell in the z direction and set the front and back patches to empty.
Let D be the nozzle inlet width, for example D = 0.01 m.
Use a rectangular domain extending 40D downstream from the inlet and 20D in the radial direction.
Place the nozzle inlet slot of width D centered on the left boundary and make the rest of the left boundary a solid wall.
Set the top, bottom, and right boundaries as far-field outlet boundaries.
Set the internal field to U = (0 0 0) m/s, p = 101325 Pa, and T = 300 K.
Set the inlet boundary to U = (686 0 0) m/s, p = 101325 Pa, and T = 300 K with fixedValue conditions.
Set the far-field outlet boundaries to waveTransmissive for p and T and zeroGradient for U.
Set the solid wall boundaries to noSlip for U, zeroGradient for p, and zeroGradient for T.
Run the simulation as a viscous laminar case with no turbulence model.
Set the front and back boundaries to empty in constant/polyMesh/boundary.
In system/controlDict, set application to rhoCentralFoam.
Run the simulation transiently with a Courant number below 1.
